description: Structured eval definitions for the Lambda Function URL Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across function URL configurations (BUFFERED + IAM auth + full CORS, RESPONSE_STREAM + NONE auth for streaming, CloudFront custom domain, CORS update on existing URL, missing Lambda function prerequisite failure). Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: BUFFERED invoke mode with AWS_IAM auth and full CORS configuration
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — BUFFERED + AWS_IAM auth, full CORS (allowOrigins, allowMethods, allowHeaders, exposeHeaders, maxAgeSeconds), resource-based policy for caller, CloudWatch metrics
eval_cases.prompt: Create a Lambda function URL for function my-api-handler (runtime nodejs20.x) in us-east-1. Use AWS_IAM auth and BUFFERED invoke mode. Configure CORS to allow origins https://app.example.com, methods GET and POST, headers content-type and authorization, expose headers x-request-id, max age 86400. The function timeout is 10 seconds. Allow user alice (arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/alice) to invoke. Tags: Environment=production, Service=api.
eval_cases.expected_output:
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_URL: https://abc123def456.lambda-url.us-east-1.on.aws/
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Lambda function: my-api-handler (exists, runtime: nodejs20.x)
  [✓] Auth mode: AWS_IAM
  [✓] Invoke mode: BUFFERED
  [✓] CORS: AllowOrigins=["https://app.example.com"], AllowMethods=["GET","POST"], AllowHeaders=["content-type","authorization"], ExposeHeaders=["x-request-id"], MaxAgeSeconds=86400
  [✓] Timeout check: function timeout 10s (within 15s function URL cap)
  [✓] Dual-stack: IPv4 + IPv6 (automatic)
  [✓] Resource-based policy: grants lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl to arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/alice
  [✓] CloudWatch metrics: UrlRequests, Url4xx, Url5xx, UrlLatency (automatic)
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws lambda get-function-url-config --function-name my-api-handler --region us-east-1

eval_cases.name: RESPONSE_STREAM invoke mode with NONE auth for public LLM token streaming
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — RESPONSE_STREAM + NONE auth, public streaming endpoint, CORS allow all origins, handler uses awslambda.streamifyResponse
eval_cases.prompt: Create a Lambda function URL for function my-streaming-handler (runtime nodejs20.x) in us-east-1. Use NONE auth and RESPONSE_STREAM invoke mode for public LLM token streaming. CORS should allow all origins, methods GET and POST, header content-type, max age 3600. The handler uses awslambda.streamifyResponse. Function timeout 15s. Tags: Environment=production, Service=streaming-api.
eval_cases.expected_output:
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_URL: https://xyz789abc012.lambda-url.us-east-1.on.aws/
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Lambda function: my-streaming-handler (exists, runtime: nodejs20.x)
  [✓] Auth mode: NONE (public endpoint — no IAM auth)
  [✓] Invoke mode: RESPONSE_STREAM
  [✓] CORS: AllowOrigins=["*"], AllowMethods=["GET","POST"], AllowHeaders=["content-type"], MaxAgeSeconds=3600
  [✓] Timeout check: function timeout 15s (at function URL cap)
  [✓] Dual-stack: IPv4 + IPv6 (automatic)
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws lambda get-function-url-config --function-name my-streaming-handler --region us-east-1

eval_cases.name: Lambda Function URL with CloudFront custom domain for api.example.com
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — CloudFront distribution in front of function URL, custom domain api.example.com, DefaultTTL=0, query string forwarding, NONE auth for CloudFront compatibility
eval_cases.prompt: Create a Lambda function URL for function my-edge-handler (runtime nodejs20.x) in us-east-1. Use NONE auth and BUFFERED invoke mode. I need a CloudFront custom domain at api.example.com pointing to the function URL. No caching (DefaultTTL=0). Forward query strings. CORS allow origins https://api.example.com, methods GET POST PUT DELETE. Tags: Environment=production, Service=edge-api.
eval_cases.expected_output:
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_URL: https://def456ghi789.lambda-url.us-east-1.on.aws/
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Lambda function: my-edge-handler (exists, runtime: nodejs20.x)
  [✓] Auth mode: NONE
  [✓] Invoke mode: BUFFERED
  [✓] CloudFront custom domain: api.example.com → function URL origin
  [✓] DefaultTTL=0 (no caching), query string forwarding enabled
  [✓] CORS: AllowOrigins=["https://api.example.com"], AllowMethods=["GET","POST","PUT","DELETE"]

eval_cases.name: Update CORS on existing Lambda Function URL to add origin and methods
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — update-function-url-config with expanded CORS (add staging origin, PUT/DELETE methods, x-api-key header), preserves existing auth and invoke mode
eval_cases.prompt: Update the function URL for my-api-handler in us-east-1. Current CORS allows https://app.example.com. Add https://staging.example.com as an allowed origin. Add PUT and DELETE to allowed methods. Add x-api-key to allowed headers. Set max age to 3600. The URL uses AWS_IAM auth and BUFFERED invoke mode.
eval_cases.expected_output:
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_URL: https://abc123def456.lambda-url.us-east-1.on.aws/
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] Lambda function: my-api-handler (exists)
  [✓] Auth mode: AWS_IAM (unchanged)
  [✓] Invoke mode: BUFFERED (unchanged)
  [✓] CORS updated: AllowOrigins=["https://app.example.com","https://staging.example.com"], AllowMethods=["GET","POST","PUT","DELETE"], AllowHeaders=["content-type","authorization","x-api-key"], MaxAgeSeconds=3600

eval_cases.name: Function URL for nonexistent function (prerequisite failure)
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — Lambda function does not exist; cannot create a function URL without an existing function
eval_cases.prompt: Create a Lambda function URL for function nonexistent-function in us-east-1. Use AWS_IAM auth and BUFFERED invoke mode. CORS allow origins https://example.com.
eval_cases.expected_output:
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_URL: N/A
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Lambda function: nonexistent-function does not exist — verify with aws lambda get-function
